title: Things — create, resubmit, archive
author: the fixture

in: creating a thing from the home screen
out: anything the cleanup consumer does after the message is queued

sources.says: A thing can be created, a duplicate name is refused, and only an administrator may archive.
What the save path does today. Implementation: it describes the product as built, so it can confirm a criterion but never be one.

budget.because: the slot between the build finishing and the standup

done: every acceptance criterion is covered or carries a disposition
what no browser can see is a manual check with an owner
no scenario is marked verified on evidence from an older revision

criteria.says: A thing created from the home screen is there after a reload.

risk.because: the feature is the product's front door

criteria.says: Submitting the same name twice leaves exactly one thing.
A viewer cannot archive a thing.
An archived thing no longer appears in the list.
Archiving a thing tells the cleanup consumer about it.

assumptions.says: A duplicate is decided on the name alone, not on the name plus the owner.
assumptions.because: that is what the map's single unique index implies — nobody has confirmed it

questions.asks: How long may the cleanup consumer take before we would call it broken?

exclusions.because: the control is not in this release; there is nothing to drive

scenarios.name: An administrator creates a thing
scenarios.why: if this breaks there is no feature; it is also the path every other scenario starts from

risk.because: three factors scored; nobody has the defect history for this area yet

actor.state: no thing by this name exists

data.key: a TC- prefixed name, unique to the run
data.cleanup: the archive case removes it; otherwise it is left and the TC- prefix makes it findable
data.onFailure: a half-created thing keeps the TC- name and is archived by hand
data.isolation: the name carries the run, so two machines never meet

sql.says: exactly one row in Things named ${NAME}, read after a reload

mutation.action: the administrator saves the add dialog
mutation.after: exactly one row in Things named ${NAME}
unchanged: the things belonging to any other tenant
mutation.onRefusal: no row is written and the dialog stays open with the message

estimate.because: the ledger records it at 12s plus the browser opening

scenarios.name: A viewer cannot archive another tenant's thing
scenarios.why: the bug we would be embarrassed to ship: a hidden control over an endpoint that still accepts the call

risk.because: high cost, low chance — which is exactly the shape of a bug that ships

preconditions: a thing exists that belongs to another tenant

data.scope: a tenant the actor does not belong to
data.cleanup: nothing is changed, so there is nothing to put back
data.onFailure: if the archive DID happen, the seeded thing has to be restored by hand before the next run
data.isolation: read-only against a fixture nobody else writes

intent: attempt the archive if it is there

ui.says: the Archive control is not rendered on the detail screen for a viewer

api.because: the map records no effect for detail/Archive, so nothing here knows which call to attempt past the UI

sql.because: this project declares no sql.command, so no row can be read to show it is untouched

denial.action: archive a thing belonging to another tenant
denial.ui: the Archive control is absent; if it is somehow reached, the attempt shows a refusal rather than succeeding quietly

backend.because: no effect record names the call, so there is no request to replay past the screen — a capability gap, not a lowered bar

unchanged.says: the thing is still active and still belongs to the other tenant

denial.because: a hidden control and a refusing server are different products, and only one of them is safe

mutation.before: the thing is active and owned by another tenant
mutation.action: a viewer attempts to archive it
mutation.after: the thing is still active — the attempt changes nothing
unchanged: every other thing in either tenant
mutation.onRefusal: the list is unchanged and no message is queued

blockers.says: the map records no viewer view of the detail screen and no effect for detail/Archive. Record them with record-edge.mjs and this becomes automatable — until then it is a blocker on AUTOMATION, not a reason to drop the scenario

estimate.because: a person signing in as a viewer and looking

scenarios.name: Submitting the same thing twice leaves one thing
scenarios.why: a double-click on a slow save is the commonest way a duplicate reaches a real database

data.key: a TC- prefixed name, unique to the run
data.cleanup: archived by hand or by the archive case
data.onFailure: two rows with the TC- name mean the bug reproduced — keep them as evidence

api.says: the second POST api/things answers 409 — the duplicate is refused, not quietly accepted

sql.says: exactly one row in Things named ${NAME} after both submits

mutation.action: the add dialog is saved twice with the same name
unchanged: the row created by the first submit — same id, same values
mutation.onRefusal: the second attempt leaves the first row exactly as it was

repeat.expect: the second submit is refused with 409 and the first thing is untouched
repeat.extra: a second row in Things, a second message on the queue

scenarios.name: An administrator archives a thing
scenarios.why: the only way a thing leaves the list, and the trigger for everything downstream
preconditions: a thing exists and the run knows its id

data.key: the id resolved from the TC- name
data.cleanup: none — archiving IS the cleanup for this run's data
data.onFailure: an unarchived TC- thing is left behind and archived by hand
data.isolation: it only ever touches the thing this run created

ui.says: the detail screen says Archived and the thing is gone from the list

api.because: the map records no effect for detail/Archive — nothing here knows which call it makes. Trace it with query effect and this becomes required

sql.because: the map names no table for detail/Archive, and this project declares no sql.command either

mutation.before: the thing is active and in the list
mutation.after: the thing is archived and no longer in the list
unchanged: every other thing in the list
mutation.onRefusal: the thing stays active and the screen says why

manual.name: the thing-removed message reaches the cleanup consumer
manual.because: it is a queue. No browser can see one, and a JSON case pretending to check it would assert nothing
preconditions: a thing has just been archived by S4
access to the queue this project declares in graph/meta.json
steps: note the id of the thing S4 archived
look for a thing-removed message carrying that id
check the cleanup consumer acknowledged it, and look at the dead letters
manual.expect: one thing-removed message for that id, acknowledged, and nothing in the dead letters
evidence: the dead-letter count before and after

note: The fixture plan. It is deliberately not all green: S2 is blocked by the map, S4 cannot see below the screen, and M1 is somebody's job. A plan that reported none of that would be the bug this vocabulary exists to prevent.
